We are writing a fan fiction in the FMAB universe. Here is the story so far:

Name: Ren Jinhai (“compassionate ocean of knowledge”)

Age: 18

Origin: Xingian prince, coming to Amestris under pressure of the succession conflict, but more interested in expanding his knowledge.

Personality traits: Driven, curious, introverted, composed, compassionate, empathetic, and intelligent

Backstory: Ren Jinhai was a prodigy in Alkahestry at a young age. When he was 8, his mother, with whom he was very close, passed away due to an illness. This ignited his interest in studying human transmutation, but he eventually learned from witnessing the Truth that it was impossible to bring a soul back. Through his research, he invented the unique ability to enter the Truth portal through meditation, which allows him to perform remote transmutations without a matrix.

Abilities: Ren Jinhai is a prodigy in Alkahestry and has the unique ability to enter the Truth portal through meditation. This combination allows him to perform remote transmutations without a matrix, making his alkahestry more similar to Hohenheim’s alchemy, albeit without a philosopher’s stone.

Motivations: Ren Jinhai is primarily motivated by his desire to expand his knowledge and abilities as an alkahestrist. He is also driven by his compassion for others and a desire to use his abilities to help those in need.

Chapter 1:

Ren Jinhai had been traveling for weeks, his thoughts consumed with the prospect of expanding his knowledge in Amestris. He had left behind his life as a Xingian prince and his family’s political struggles in the hopes of finding something more meaningful in this foreign land. As he approached the outskirts of Rush Valley, he felt a sense of excitement and anticipation rising within him.

<This is it. The land of automail, where my knowledge of alkahestry can intersect with automail engineering.>

Meanwhile, Winry Rockbell was working in her shop, lost in the rhythm of her craft. She was focused on the task at hand, carefully threading wires through a complex network of metal joints and gears. She loved the precision and intricacy of automail engineering, and the feeling of satisfaction that came with a job well done.

<Just a little more…there! That should do it.>

As Ren approached the entrance to Winry’s shop, he paused to take in the sight of the bustling town. The sound of clanking metal and the smell of oil filled his senses, and he felt a sense of awe at the sheer ingenuity of the automail technology on display.

<So this is Rush Valley…it truly lives up to its reputation.>
Winry looked up from her work as the door to her shop opened, and she saw a tall, dark-haired man enter. She felt a momentary flutter in her chest at the sight of him, but quickly pushed the thought aside.

<Who is this guy? He looks lost.>

Ren approached the counter where Winry was standing, and their eyes met for a moment. He felt a jolt of recognition, as if he had met her before.

<Who is this girl? Her eyes…they’re so familiar.>

“Excuse me,” he said, his voice low and smooth. “I’m looking for someone who can help me with automail.”

Winry smiled brightly, feeling a warmth spread through her chest at the sound of his voice.

“That’s me! I’m Winry Rockbell, the best automail mechanic in Amestris. What can I do for you?”

Ren felt a sense of relief wash over him at her friendly demeanor.

<She seems nice. And competent.>
“I’m Ren Jinhai,” he said, extending his hand. “I’m a newcomer to Amestris, and I’m interested in learning more about automail engineering. Would you be willing to show me around?”

Winry’s heart skipped a beat as she took his hand, feeling a surge of electricity pass between them.

<Wow, he’s…charming. And handsome.>

“Sure, I’d love to show you around,” she said, feeling a flush spread across her cheeks. “Let me grab my tools, and we can get started.”

As the two set off into the bustling town, Ren felt a sense of excitement building within him. He had come to Amestris in search of knowledge, but he had a feeling that he might have just found something more.

As they walked through the streets of Rush Valley, Ren and Winry chatted amicably, their conversation flowing effortlessly. They talked about their shared love of automail engineering and alkahestry, and Ren found himself feeling more and more drawn to the bright, enthusiastic young woman beside him.

<She’s so…vibrant. And talented. I could learn so much from her.>

Winry, for her part, found herself enjoying Ren’s company more than she had expected. His quiet intelligence and easy charm were refreshing after years of dealing with loud, boisterous automail engineers.

<He’s different. And I like it.>

As they made their way through the town, Ren and Winry stopped at several automail shops, and Ren watched with fascination as Winry demonstrated her skills. He was struck by the precision and attention to detail she brought to her work, and he found himself feeling grateful for the opportunity to learn from her.

<She’s a true artist. And a patient teacher.>

Winry, in turn, was impressed by Ren’s curiosity and his willingness to learn. She could sense a deep passion for knowledge in him, and she found herself wanting to help him however she could.

<He’s eager to learn. And he’s so…focused.>

As the afternoon wore on, Ren and Winry found themselves sitting in a small café, sipping coffee and talking about their dreams and aspirations. Ren spoke about his desire to unlock the secrets of alkahestry and to use his knowledge to help others, while Winry shared her hopes of one day becoming the best automail engineer in the world.

<We’re not so different, after all.>

As they said their goodbyes, Ren felt a sense of regret that their time together had come to an end.

<I don’t want to leave her side. There’s something…special about her.>

Winry, too, felt a pang of sadness as she watched Ren walk away.

<He’s…intriguing. And charming.>

As the sun began to set over Rush Valley, both Ren and Winry found themselves lost in their own thoughts, their minds filled with visions of what the future might hold. They knew that their paths would cross again, and they couldn’t wait to see what destiny had in store for them.

Ren paused for a moment, taking a deep breath before speaking. He knew he was taking a risk, but he couldn’t help the way he felt.

“Winry,” he said, his voice steady and sure. “I know this is our first meeting, but I can’t deny that I feel a connection with you. You’re so talented and passionate, and I can’t help but be drawn to that. Would it be too forward of me to ask if I could come over tomorrow too? I want to learn from you, and I…I want to get to know you better.”

Winry was taken aback by Ren’s words, but she couldn’t help the flutter in her stomach at the thought of spending more time with him.

“Really?” she asked, her eyes wide with surprise. “You want to come over again?”

Ren nodded, a small smile playing at the corners of his mouth.

“I do,” he said. “I know it’s a lot to ask, but I can’t help the way I feel.”

Winry’s heart skipped a beat at the sincerity in Ren’s voice, and she found herself nodding before she could even think.

“Yes,” she said. “I’d like that. I want to get to know you better too.”

As they said their goodbyes, both Ren and Winry felt a sense of excitement and anticipation building inside of them. They knew that tomorrow would be the start of something new and wonderful, and they couldn’t wait to see where their connection would lead them.

Ren arrived at Winry’s shop the next day, his heart pounding with anticipation as he walked through the door. Winry greeted him with a smile, and they set to work on a new project together. As they worked, Ren found himself drawn to Winry’s passion and drive, and he couldn’t help but feel a sense of admiration and respect for her.

<He is so different from Ed>, Winry thought to herself as she watched Ren work. <Ed was always so brash and reckless, never thinking things through. But Ren…Ren is careful, considerate.>

As they worked, Ren found himself opening up to Winry, telling her about his past and his struggles to find his place in the world.

“I was always different from the other Xingians,” he said. “I was interested in things like alchemy and science, while they were more focused on politics and power. When I lost my mother, I felt so lost and alone. But I knew that I had to keep going, to find a way to make sense of everything. That’s when I started studying human transmutation, trying to find a way to bring her back.”

Winry listened with rapt attention as Ren spoke, feeling a sense of compassion and empathy for him.

“I know how that feels,” she said softly. “I lost my parents too, and it was the worst thing that ever happened to me. But you can’t bring them back, Ren. You have to find a way to live with the pain and move forward.”

Ren nodded, a sense of gratitude and respect for Winry welling up inside of him.

“You’re right,” he said. “I’ve come to realize that now. But I still want to keep learning, to keep growing. And I think I can do that here, with you.”

Winry smiled, feeling a sense of warmth and connection with Ren.

“I think you can too,” she said.

As they worked, Ren found himself drawn to Winry more and more, and he couldn’t help but feel a sense of attraction and desire building inside of him. He wanted to touch her, to feel her skin against his, to taste her lips and lose himself in her.

<Is it too soon?>, he wondered to himself. <Will she think I’m moving too fast?>

Meanwhile, Winry was feeling a similar sense of desire and attraction towards Ren, her body humming with anticipation and need.

<God, he’s so gorgeous>, she thought to herself as she watched him work. <I can’t believe I’m feeling this way about someone I just met.>

As they worked, their bodies grew closer and closer, until they were practically touching. And then, without warning, Ren leaned in and pressed his lips to hers.

As the space between them grew smaller, Ren’s pulse quickened, the anticipation causing his palms to feel clammy. <What will her lips feel like?> The thought wrought a wave of longing through his body. Winry’s breath hitched, feeling like a warm breeze brushed through her nerves as their faces drew closer. <What will his touch bring?>

Their lips met, softly at first, like the gentle grazing of butterfly wings. An electrifying jolt surged through them, awakening an exquisite symphony of desire. Encouraged, their mouths pressed more firmly against each other, eliciting from them small involuntary sighs that resonated in the air around them.

Ren marveled at the sensation of Winry’s full, tender lips as his heart raced. Her taste was subtly sweet and intoxicating, making him crave more. Their gentle explorations intensified, their mouths pressing harder, lips sliding against one another with growing fervor. In Query-Focused Video Summarization, the summarization process is conditioned on an input user
query, thus, multiple summaries can be obtained for the same video using different input queries.
Dataset. We evaluate our method on the QFVS dataset based on the UT Egocentric videos described
earlier. The dataset consists of 46 queries for each of the four videos and user-annotated video
summaries for each query.
Quantitative Results. In Tab. 6, we compare F1 scores of our method to 3 baselines, SH-DPP [32],
Seq-DPP [5], and QFVS [33]. Following [33], we run four rounds of experiments leaving out one
video for testing and one for validation, while keeping the remaining two for training. Our full model
achieves an avg F1 score of 54.55% outperforming the best baseline (44.19%) by 10%. We would like
to point out that our method uses more recent image features compared to the baselines. At the same
time, when switching from CLIP to ResNet image embedding, we still improve significantly over the
baselines. We expect the improvement to also hold with weaker features (e.g., as demonstrated with
GoogleNet results in Tab. 1, 2).
Qualitative Results. Fig. 5 shows a result on the QFVS dataset for UT Egocentric videos. The input
is an egocentric video shot from a head-mounted camera and spans 4 hours. It consists of multiple
events from a person’s day, such as reading books, working on the laptop, walking in the streets, and
so on. Summary 1 and 2 show results from our CLIP-It method when the input query is “Book and
chair” and “Sun and tree” respectively. The frames shown are frames assigned high-scores by our

Create a 2 page note on Understanding Shares
Share repurchases:
Compensation through shares (e.g. stock options)
Stock splits and the different methods for shares
steps:
assistant: # Understanding Shares

## Page 1:

**Introduction to Shares**

Shares represent units of ownership interest in a company or financial asset that provide for an equal distribution in any profits, if any are declared, in the form of dividends. When individuals or entities purchase shares, they become shareholders or stockholders of the corporation, giving them various rights including claims on part of the company’s assets and earnings.

**Types of Shares**

1. **Common Shares**: These are the most frequently issued type of shares that confer voting rights to shareholders, allowing them to vote on company issues and board elections. Common shareholders, however, are at the end of the priority line for company assets.

2. **Preferred Shares**: These shares often do not provide voting rights, but they do grant shareholders a higher claim on assets and earnings than common shareholders, including fixed dividends.

**Share Repurchases**

A share repurchase, or buyback, occurs when a company buys its own outstanding shares to reduce the number of shares available on the open market. Reasons for share repurchases include:

- **Ownership Consolidation**: Reducing the number of shares outstanding increases remaining shareholders' relative ownership stakes.

- **Undervaluation Signal**: Companies may buy back shares if leadership believes they are undervalued.

- **Earnings Per Share (EPS) Boost**: Fewer outstanding shares increase the EPS, which can make a company appear more profitable and increase the stock price.

- **Excess Cash**: A repurchase can be a way to utilize excess cash in lieu of other investment opportunities.

**Risks and Criticisms of Share Repurchases**

- Can be perceived as a lack of growth opportunities or productive investments.
- May lead to artificial inflation of stock prices.
- Can divest funds that might be used for company development or employee compensation.

**Stock Buybacks Regulation**

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulates repurchase programs with Rule 10b-18, which provides a "safe harbor" for companies to repurchase their shares without being accused of market manipulation.

## Page 2:

**Compensation through Shares**

1. **Stock Options**: These give employees the option to buy company stock at a future date at a predetermined price (often less than the current market value). It incentivizes employees to improve company performance because their potential profit increases with the company's stock price.

2. **Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)**: These are a promise to grant a set number of shares of the company's stock to the employee upon the completion of the vesting schedule. They motivate employees to stay with the company and contribute to its success.

3. **Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPPs)**: This program allows employees to purchase company stock at a discounted price, often through payroll deductions over a specific offering period.

**Stock Splits and Methods**

- **Traditional Stock Split**: A company increases the number of its outstanding shares by a specific multiple to lower the price of each individual share, making it more accessible to investors but does not change the market capitalization or the value of the company.

- **Reverse Stock Split**: It consolidates the number of existing shares of stock into fewer shares, raising the price of the individual shares. It's often used to prevent delisting from stock exchanges that have minimum share price requirements.

- **Bonus Issue (Stock Dividend)**: This is a dividend payment made in the form of additional shares rather than a cash payout. Similar to a traditional stock split, it makes the share price more accessible.

**Impact of Stock Splits and Bonus Issues**

- Generally perceived positively as they show that the company is growing and is confident in future earnings.
- The affordability of shares may attract more retail investors.
- May signal a buying opportunity to the market, often resulting in short-term share price increases.
- Has no direct impact on the company’s fundamentals but can influence perceptions and stock liquidity.

**Conclusion**

Understanding shares is critical for investors and company employees alike, as shares represent the value, ownership, and potential profit of being part of a corporation. From deciding on voting in shareholder meetings to comprehending the implications of share repurchases and stock compensations, a solid grasp of shares is a foundation to better decision-making in the world of finance and corporate governance.

But we’ll be alright; I promise you. Despite all your suffering, you’re still far more resilient than your old man” He paused, suddenly feeling his mere twenty six years of life weighing on his frame as he offered equilibrium to her dependent, innocent youth as she gazed up at him . Her hazel irises stared intently into his matching brown and amber aspect, and a smile crossed his lips. “My God, I can’t believe you’re already two-days old, and rest assured sweetheart, you’re the most precious thing I have in this world. “ His voice trailed off, as his gaze lingered on her translucent skin, her veins shining under the soft light. “And you’re so gorgeous, so incomprehensible I— I can’t quite believe you are alive. A little fighter, and brave as hell, too.”

Exhausted but at peace with her fitting perfectly between his wrist and forearm, he sighed with a profound sense of fulfilment and redemption. Standing placated in the encroaching dusk , as he pulled her closer against his chest, his gaze drifted to the glass window beyond him.
Amidst the fading light that outlined buildings and wisps of smog, he felt a sense of perishing hope; one that he clung to with grit and resolve , if only for her sake.
As he gently traced her delicate features with his finger, she reached up and hooked her index finger over his thumb, creating a fragile but powerful lifeline , transpiring through the grim backdrop of her makeshift nursery.

“Lily bean, your mother, she-“. He hadn’t the words nor the heart to continue as her intricate grasp on his own slid away, her hand splaying across her chest as she slipped into slumber. “You can sleep, there’ll be plenty of time to stare at this mug in the morning”. He exhaled with relief and wonderment as her consciousness seemed to melt away into the bleak atmosphere. As her breathing then fell against his palm, it was a soothing rhythm. Leaving him stupefied in the peaceful lull of the ebb and flow, he muttered. “Why must you look like her? Well, you may actually resemble me and now, that’s not so great huh?” . Max smiled at her oblivion, which he prayed would not betray her someday. “Don’t you dare wake up yet” he muttered , her sleeping form realigning itself against him, seeming to sense his presence as her pulse slowed. Unable to even move, Max stood with the sleeping infant , too exhausted to lay her down in the clinical humidicrib of sallow light that hummed with a disconcerting tone. Overwrought with fatigue yet savouring the fleeting moment of solace, he willed it to engulf him in its embrace. Although it tore incremental fragments from his being, it was solace all the same.

It had been a long , dragging night of insomnia , flashbacks and a lack of food as Max leaned his spine against the hospital corridor. There he had set up vigil , not leaving the hall as he watched her in his peripheral version. “How could Elara abandon the poor kid. How could she just -“ . As he ran a calloused hand over his unshaven jaw, Max contemplated the impending call that suffocated his tattered psyche . It was the inevitability encroaching on his raw nerves as his fingers unlocked his phone with trepidation , and scrolled for her number.

“Elara? I don’t know. You discharged yourself, no I don’t care where the hell you are -she can’t survive on air. No, but please just tell me what I can do to fix -No, of course I love you, I’m alone in a hospital with our, well, my daughter.-“ The phone went dead in his ear and he let it backflip into his lap with resignation.

Returning to his haphazard scattering of belongings, he pried open an energy drink, draining and then crushing the aluminium under his fingers, the distorted metal absorbing his anguish and dismay. All of his disbelief and heartbreak over Elara seemed weightless , meaningless and forgotten as he heard Lily’s almost inaudible whimpers floating in the air. “Right here Lily, I’ve got you.” his hoarse voice found her, and her fussing stopped in an instant. His softening voice whispered intangible phrases, he half sang, his deep-throated hum off balance from his persistent fatigue. A lullaby of his own, off key, intermingling with her cries, permeated the space between them.

His eyes floated shut, and images of cowering under creaking stairs, the weight above him luring closer, his young screams pleading for mercy, filled his mind. “I didn’t mean to, Dad-“ everything grew colder, then a fierce heat drove through him, making him flinch at the recollection. A boot sailed past his head. Then a knife.

Max re-opened his eyes, back in the present once more, his pulse already thundering out of sync with his infant daughter’s, whose accelerated heartbeat still seemed calmer than his own. “I’m sorry you’ll be in here a while longer, my little bean. Can’t take you home, yet. But you’re gonna love your own crib, it’ll put this humidifier to shame. You just wait and see…” With a heavy weight in his lungs, almost drowning him with the proximity of his flashback, his mind flickered to Elara. As he held the still crying Lily, determined to soothe her discomfort in the cool night, he could still taste Elara, feel her in his clothes, and it sickened his heart. As he placed Lily into her contraption of a crib with reluctance , he sank against the wall , overcome with another whim of utter frustration and he had to fight the torrent of unfiltered torment that tore through his clenched teeth. “Pick up, please…Elara? Oh God, just tell me why-No I haven’t slept, she’s in a critical condition-don’t worry about it. I know it’s heartbreaking-Oh I’m not going through hell right now? No please I’m sorry-“.

Again, the line died out in the shell of his ear, wrenching a knife through the lining of his stomach. Exhaustion gnawed ferociously on his brain, and he relented to sleep as it finally came, like a tower of building blocks, smashing him.

“ No , Max , I -it’s because I love her that I can’t watch her suffer -“. Elara’s tearstained blue gaze pierced into his , as she stood under the harsh lights of the parking lot. Just like a deer in headlights, her frightened expression wore an acceptance of fate. Max , reaching out and grabbing her wrist, drove his pleas of incredulity into the closing space between them. “Elara , please , I love you, but I love my child, damnit…And I will be there when she takes her last breath if that’s what I have to do for her. -“” .

His pulse raced to the surface of his throat as he retched himself into stark consciousness, gazing around in sheer panic as he ran a hand over his drawn features. Upon hearing his child’s faint breathing , a newfound white noise that salved his frayed nerves , he relaxed against the wall.

Six weeks had passed and Max had been offered respite housing by the hospital, his clothes were fresh and his face clean shaven as he entered the NICU and locked eyes on his daughter.
“Morning , Gorgeous “ . The mild the mild rays of morning bleeding into the room, embracing her in a blanket of warmth, the humidicrib encasing his daughter with a plastic film of isolation. He staggered over to where she lay , and elevated her into the air . “My little girl is six weeks old . I swear you’re growing bigger every single day”. With grit under his nails and darkness pooling under his eyes , an accumulation of the passing days , he beamed at Lily with awe and relief, and pride. “Daddy passed out cold , he was so tired. But I’m here now and I’m not going anywhere kiddo.” At that moment, she gazed into his eyes , and smiled , causing his eyes to glaze over . “Of course you’re smiling, because you know I love you right?”. His daughter, in an exuberant moment free from agony, maintained her entrancing grin, and his arms trembled as he lowered her onto his forearm, holding her close. “Your first smile perhaps? I’ll have to ask the nurses…they’ve taken such phenomenal care of you. You’ll be at home before you even know it.” Her invigorated breathing, steady and strong against his skin, gave him something palpable to focus on as he lamented the grave reality, and cursed under his breath. “I miss her, you know, but I worry about her too. Maybe some day she’ll find her way back to us. But I’ll be here for your first word , first step. You’re gonna come on jogs with me huh? Yeah that’s right you are.”

steps:
assistant: Here are additional ideas for ailments and conditions to include in your RPG, each with a unique gameplay impact:

1. Confused - Character may act randomly, including targeting allies or using items incorrectly.
2. Cursed - Character takes damage or experiences negative effects when attempting certain actions, like casting spells or attacking.
3. Hexed - A specific ability or skill is locked and cannot be used until the hex is lifted.
4. Enraged - Character gains attack power but loses the ability to distinguish between friend and foe, potentially attacking allies.
5. Bleeding - Loses HP over time and may leave the character vulnerable to being tracked or attracting predators.
6. Weakened - Attacks and skills are less effective, and character may have reduced carrying capacity.
7. Diseased - Over time, multiple secondary symptoms develop, such as reduced stats, inability to heal naturally, or spreading the ailment to others.
8. Burdened - Movement speed is reduced due to over-encumbrance or an environmental effect such as mud.
9. Charmed - The character is under the influence of an enemy and may act on their behalf or be prevented from attacking them.
10. Hallucinating - The character sees illusions, including fake enemies or terrain, complicating navigation and combat.
11. Muted - The character cannot make noise, preventing them from using vocal commands or shouts.
12. Disoriented - The character's controls may be reversed or randomized for a period, making movement and targeting difficult.
13. Mana Burned - The character loses a portion of their mana pool each turn and may take damage if attempting to cast with insufficient mana.
14. Withered - Character's maximum health or another primary stat is temporarily reduced.
15. Drained - Slow loss of all resources over time, such as health, mana, and stamina.
16. Entangled - Movement is significantly restricted due to vines, webs, or similar constraints.
17. Crystallized - Defenses are enhanced but the character has a chance of shattering (taking critical damage) upon hit.
18. Infected - Similar to poisoned, but it has the potential to spread to nearby characters and may mutate into new ailments.
19. Sapped - Character loses their buffs or positive status effects over time.
20. Frenzied - Increases aggression and offensive capability, but the character cannot distinguish between low-threat and high-threat targets.
21. Overloaded - If the character uses too much magic or tech, they might become unable to act due to an overload.
22. Radiated - Suffer damage over time and contaminates nearby areas or allies until cleansed.
23. Nauseated - Character may fail to act and can throw up, potentially losing items or consumed buffs.

These conditions can add a level of strategy to your game, requiring players to think about how they manage these ailments both in and out of combat. Remember to balance these ailments properly; too many negative conditions can lead to a frustrating gameplay experience, while too few can make the game feel less challenging.

## **Mitigating Misinformation in the Digital Age: Effect of** Critical Thinking and Media Literacy **Interventions on Habitual Adaptation**

**Research Question:** *How can informed and context-aware media literacy interventions effectively disrupt habitual adaptation to algorithmic personalization, thereby mitigating the spread of misinformation and fostering a more open public sphere?*

### **Introduction**

In the current digital landscape, personalized algorithms hold a significant impact on the information we consume. This has resulted in the formation of filter bubbles, often called "echo chambers", online platforms where individuals are exposed only to content that reinforces their pre-existing beliefs, potentially leading to group polarization and therefore limiting the scope of open dialogue in the political and public discourse. The **filter bubble effect**, often associated with algorithmic personalization, has drawn significant attention due to its impact on information diversity. However, findings suggest that there is a limited understanding of the specific mechanisms underlying digital echo chambers and filter bubbles, thus focusing solely on information diversity may not be enough. A more fundamental issue that requires attention and further research is **habitual adaptation**.

Our research attempts to study how contextually-informed media literacy interventions can disrupt habitual adaptation to algorithmic personalization, reduce the spread of misinformation, and foster a more inclusive public sphere. Additionally, we aim to explore why different groups interpret the same information in varying landscapes and develop strategies to prevent ideological perspectives from becoming entrenched as partisan identities.

### Objectives

The primary objective of our research proposal is to develop and test targeted and effective strategies to entrust users with the necessary skills and knowledge to critically engage with information and counter misinformation. Specifically, our research aims to achieve the following two objectives:

1. Disrupting habitual adaptation, which refers to users' tendency to adapt to algorithmic personalization and limit their exposure to diverse perspectives. We propose to explore how tailored media literacy interventions can effectively disrupt this behaviour and encourage users to seek out diverse perspectives.
2. Mitigating misinformation spread by training users with the necessary knowledge and skills to effectively identify and counter misinformation. This will involve providing users with a comprehensive understanding of the context, content, creation, circulation, consumption, and consequences of information.

Through our research proposal, we aim to contribute to the field of media literacy and misinformation studies by providing evidence-based interventions that can effectively empower users to become critical consumers of information and counter misinformation.

### **Research Approach**

The critical questions of our research revolve around answering the following:

- *How do users habitually adapt to algorithmic personalization, and how does this impact their exposure to information within filter bubbles?*
- *What role does critical thinking play in breaking habitual patterns and promoting a more diverse information consumption?*
- *Why do different groups in society develop highly divergent personal readings of the same information? How does this result in the solidification of contrasting ideological perspectives into group polarization?*

To try and answer those questions, we will use the methodology that follows.

### **Methodology**

1. **Literature Review:** Synthesizing existing research on media literacy, algorithmic personalization, and misinformation, we will identify gaps and build upon prior knowledge. Understanding the nuances of filter bubbles and user adaptation patterns will inform our intervention design.
2. **Mixed-Methods Approach:** Surveys, interviews, and behavioural experiments will help explore user behaviour within personalized content ecosystems. Quantitative analysis will measure adaptation patterns, while qualitative insights will enhance our understanding of user experiences.
3. **Intervention Design:** Collaborating with experts, we will create context-aware media literacy modules. These interventions will address misinformation, promote critical thinking, and encourage information diversity.
4. **Participant Recruitment:** Recruiting diverse participants ensures representation across demographics and political ideologies. Their insights will enrich our findings.
5. **Data Collection and Analysis:** Administering pre- and post-intervention assessments, we will analyze data using statistical methods and thematic coding. Ethical considerations guide our research.

Homiletics, the art of preaching or writing sermons, is a skill that can be developed with practice and dedication. Below is a step-by-step guide to help you craft engaging sermons:

### 1. Prayer and Spiritual Preparation
- **Seek Guidance:** Begin with prayer, asking God for wisdom, insight, and the Holy Spirit's guidance as you prepare your sermon.
- **Spiritual Readiness:** Ensure you are spiritually prepared and in a right relationship with God, allowing His word to impact you first.

### 2. Select the Scripture
- **Prayerful Selection:** Choose a scripture passage prayerfully. Let the Holy Spirit guide you to a passage that is relevant for your congregation’s current needs or follows the liturgical calendar or sermon series theme.
- **Contextual Understanding:** Understand the historical, cultural, and literary context of the passage. This depth of understanding is crucial for accurate interpretation and application.

### 3. Exegetical Work
- **Analyze the Passage:** Break down the passage, looking at the original language, literary structure, and its place within the broader narrative of Scripture.
- **Interpretation:** Interpret the main theological themes and messages of the passage based on your analysis, always aiming to stay true to the text's original meaning.

### 4. Formulate the Main Idea
- **Central Message:** Synthesize your interpretation into one central message or big idea that will be the focus of your sermon.
- **Relevance:** Consider why this message matters today and how it applies to the daily lives of your congregation.

### 5. Organize the Sermon Structure
- **Introduction:** Begin with an engaging introduction that captures attention, introduces the main theme, and creates a need for the message.
- **Body:** Organize the body around key points that support the sermon’s main idea. Use illustrations, examples, and research to add depth and interest.
- **Conclusion:** Conclude with a powerful and memorable ending that calls for a response from the congregation, whether that be reflection, repentance, or action.

### 6. Incorporate Illustrations and Applications
- **Illustrations:** Use stories, analogies, and testimonies to bring biblical truths to life.
- **Applications:** Clearly articulate how your congregation can apply the sermon’s message in their daily lives. Practical applications help the sermon to be engaging and memorable.

### 7. Practice Delivery
- **Preparation:** Practice your sermon multiple times, focusing on delivery, timing, and transitions.
- **Authenticity and Passion:** Deliver your sermon authentically, letting your passion for God’s word shine through. This connection is vital for engaging your audience.

### 8. Seek Feedback and Reflect
- **Peer Feedback:** If possible, get feedback on your sermon from trusted peers or mentors before you preach it.
- **Self-reflection:** After delivering your sermon, take time to reflect on what worked well and what could be improved for next time.

### 9. Continuous Learning
- **Study Homiletics:** Continue studying preaching and communication skills to improve constantly.
- **Spiritual Growth:** Deepen your spiritual life, as your personal walk with God will always be the foundation of your preaching.

### Conclusion
Crafting engaging Christian sermons is a sacred responsibility that requires a blend of spiritual devotion, rigorous study, and creative communication. By following these steps and committing each sermon to God in prayer, you can effectively share God’s Word in a way that transforms lives.

popular cultureThe 12 Most Underrated Marvel Characters(Twentieth Century Fox)By: Justin CohenPublished Nov 17, 2022 6:00pmThe Marvel Universe is one of the most robust and expansive comic-book universes to exist. First founded in 1939, Marvel Comics has over 70,000 characters throughout its history and multiverses, with somewhere around 8,000 staple lead characters. With such an overwhelming roster of caped crusaders to keep track of, there's bound to be a bunch of lesser-known characters that are considered underrated Marvel characters.RELATEDFrom the MCU all the way to the first live-action Marvel movie with Captain America in 1944, we’ve seen some heroes significantly more than others on the big screen. Even when some of our favorite characters make it to the movies, they don’t always get the character arc they deserve. Here is our list of the most underrated Marvel characters we think deserve their roses.1.) She-HulkAlthough She-Hulk may have gotten her own show in the MCU, Jennifer Walters remains one of the most under-appreciated characters. Vastly popular among fans, She-Hulk first appeared in The Savage She-Hulk #1 released in 1980. She-Hulk is known for constantly breaking the fourth wall and poking holes at the many superhero tropes.
Universal Television was banking off the major success of their Incredible Hulk and Bionic Woman T.V. series. Marvel became nervous that Universal Television might introduce a female version of the Hulk to their show, so they created their own version first so they'd own the rights. This explains the signature fourth-wall break that She-Hulk has become well-known for. 2.) Brother VoodooBrother Voodoo is not an unknown marvel character, but most casual fans know nothing about him or his origin. Brother Voodoo first appeared in Strange Tales #169, released in 1973. After becoming a psychologist in the United States, Jericho Drumm returns to his homeland of Haiti. He finds his brother, a male priest of voodoo, is dying from a spirit he possessed. Before he dies, Jericho vows to his brother that he will visit his mentor Loa Damballa, where he will eventually become Brother Voodoo. In comics, Brother Voodoo will eventually become the sorcery supreme after Dr.Strange's death and is renamed Doctor Voodoo. The first rumor of Brother Voodoo joining the MCU came in Dr.Strange when it was revealed one of the people Kaecilius kills was Daniel Drumm. Black Panther: Wakanda Forever also teased some of the heroes claiming Haiti as their temporary home, the same location we know Brother Voodoo is from. 3.) Silver SurferOne of the most well-known Marvel characters in my mind remains one of the most underrated, the Silver Surfer. First appearing in Fantastic Four #48, released in 1966, Silver Surfer has remained one of the most iconic characters in the Marvel universe.Norrin Konn was born on the planet Zenn-la, home to a long-lived technologically advanced humanoid race. When Galactus broke through the planet's defense systems, he came with the intention to consume the planet. Konn comes to the rescue and offers to be Galactus's personal herald and seek out planets for him to consume. Galactus agrees and turns him into the Silver Surfer. Although this may seem like the Silver Surfer is a villain, he is actually one of the noblest characters in the Marvel Universe. He tried to only lead Galactus to planets that are void of sentient life, but after it became increasingly hard to find them, he would plot a way to end Galactus's reign forever. 4.) Adam WarlockAdam Warlock may be underrated now, but with Will Poulter set to play the character in the upcoming third installment of the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise, that may change soon. He first appeared in Fantastic Four #66-67, released in 1967. Adam Warlock was created by researchers on earth known as the Enclave, whose goal was to create the perfect human being. He is most known for his role with the Infinity Gauntlet and for stopping Thanos. He was able to yield the Infinity Gauntlet before ultimately splitting up the gems so that no one person had control of all that power. It should be interesting to see what role he will exactly play in the MCU. 5.) Monica Rambeau's Captain MarvelMonica Rambeau may have had her formal introduction into the MCU, but that rendition of the character does do justice to its comic-book counterpart. Monica Rambeau first appeared in The Amazing Spider-man Annual #16, released in 1982, and is introduced as the second Captain Marvel. While trying to stop an extra-dimensional weapon, Rambeau is exposed to the special energy and thus became capable of turning her body into energy. Although her name was given to her by the media, it turned out that there was a Kree hero named Mar-Vell, who was the first Captain Marvel. Rambeau then goes to the Avengers for help in mastering her newfound powers. After being taken under the wing of Captain America and the Wasp, Rambeau graduates as an Avengers member before ultimately becoming their leader. It's very possible we one day see Monica Rambeau commanding the Avengers of the MCU. 6.) Cosmo the SpaceDog The adorable dog in a spacesuit we see in Guardians of the Galaxy may look like a device to add humor to the movie, but that is actually Cosmo the SpaceDog. Cosmo first appeared in Nova vol. 4 #8, released in 2008. Cosmo was a space dog used by the soviets during the 1960s and was launched into Earth's orbit. He would become lost in space before ending up in Knowhere. While the Guardians use Knowhere as their base for a short period Cosmo tags along for a number of adventures. We aren't sure how much screen time Cosmos may get in the future but one thing remains, everyone loves a talking space dog. 7.) TaskmasterTaskmaster is another character who has been fully introduced to the MCU but wasn't given the character arc they deserved. First appearing in The Avengers #195, released in 1980, Taskmaster is one of the most deadly hand-to-hand fighters in the Marvel universe. We may now know the full backstory of Taskmaster, but we do know what he's capable of. Taskmaster has what can be described as photographic reflexes. He can mimic and copy the exact physical movements of anyone he sees. This makes him one of the toughest foes in the Marvel universe because he is the equivalent of fighting yourself in hand-to-hand combat. Taskmaster's amazing ability suite and endearing combative personality earn him all the love in the world on this collection of the most underrated Marvel characters.8.) Squirrel Girl If you've never heard of the unbeatable Squirrel Girl then you're in for a treat. Squirrel Girl First appeared in Marvel Super-Heroes vol.2 #8, released in 1991, and was created because Marvel wanted to branch off into lighter stories than the normally dramatic tales. Doreen Allene Green, better known as Squirrel Girl, first discovered she could communicate with squirrels at the age of 10. It's later revealed that she possesses squirrel-like abilities. She actually remains an incredibly tough hero defeating the likes of M.O.D.O.K., Thanos, and even taking down the Avengers at one point. 9.) Nova The Nova Corps in the MCU may seem like a rag-tag group of dim-witted police offers, but they are quite the opposite in the comics. Nova first appeared in The Man Called Nova #1, released in 1976.
As the last great Nova Corps member from Xandar is dying, he is tasked with selecting a replacement. At random he chose high school student Richard Rider, who would become Nova. He has powers such as superhuman strength, flight, and control the powerful suite of abilities tied to the Nova force.10.) Magik Magik is undoubtedly one of the most complex and powerful heroes ever seen in the Marvel universe. She first appeared in Giant-Size X-Men #1, released in 1975. Illyana Rasputin, better known as Magik, was a mutant born in Siberia, Russia. She is the sister to notable mutants Mikhail and Colossus. At a young age, she is brought into Limbo by the ancient evil sorcerer Belasco. She is raised there and develops several magical abilities. As her character continues to grow, she must battle the demons of her youth in Limbo while trying to be the hero she wants to be. Magik and her massive "Soulsword" also make her worthy of making this list of the most underrated Marvel characters.11.) Moon Knight The Disney+ series Moon Knight was a great success and a wonderful addition to the MCU, but there is still so much about the character that went unseen. Moon Knight first appeared in Werewolf by Night #32, released in 1975. Although Moon Knight may not have super-human abilities 99% of the time, he is still an absolute badass. A Chicago native, Marc Spector, draws the attention of Khonshu, the moon god. He creates a psychic connection with Spector, turning him into Moon Knight. What ensues is a number of personalities that Moon Knight has to struggle with containing as he strays further and further away from who Marc Spector once was. 12.) Ant-ManIt's hard to claim Ant-Man as underrated when he is slated to have a third solo installment to the MCU, but I'm gonna try to make a case for him here the best I can! Ant-Man first appeared in Tales to Astonish #27, released in 1962. Hank Pym may be the original Ant-Man, but we are going to focus on Scott Lang's version of the hero. The former robber turned superhero, Scott Lang comes into possession of the Ant-Man suit after stealing it. He would fight alongside the Fantastic Four as well as the Avengers, becoming an integral part of the team. With how many of our favorite OG heroes have gotten the boot in the MCU I pray that we don't see Scott Lang's Ant-Man go anywhere anytime soon. This had been her secret for years, and no one else knew about it.

One evening, while attending a grand ball in her honor, Isabella’s eyes met with a handsome stranger. His name was Adam, and he was the captain of the King’s army. From that moment on, Isabella and Adam fell madly in love. They would sneak away together and go on adventures, exploring the woods and the neighboring villages.

When Bella returned to the castle, she was surprised to see Adam waiting for her. At first, she was scared that he had discovered her secret, but to her relief, he only wanted to talk. Adam told her how amazed he was by her bravery and how proud he was to be with such a strong woman. Bella was relieved that Adam had not rejected her, but also afraid that he would now expose her secret.

Over the next few days, Adam seemed distant, and Isabella began to worry. However, one night, while sipping wine under the stars, Adam told her that he knew her secret and that he loved her even more for it. From that moment on, Bella and Adam fought side by side, and their love only grew stronger.

The kingdom was never the same after that. Isabella would continue to rule during the day as a petite princess with grace and kindness, but she also had a warrior spirit deep within her that would come alive at midnight. Adam saw both aspects of Isabella and loved her for both, knowing that he found someone truly remarkable.

In the end, their love was the strongest force in the kingdom, and people would tell stories of their romance for generations to come. And in those stories, Isabella was never just a petite princess, but a warrior woman who would defend her people with all her might.

assistant: A checkcif file alert usually indicates that there is an issue with the structural data of a crystallographic file. Checkcif is a software tool that helps to verify the correctness and completeness of an uploaded crystallographic file against standard criteria. 

An alert from checkcif could suggest many things, like missing or inconsistent data, wrong symmetry, anomalous bond lengths or angles, poorly defined electron density, and so on. It is crucial to address these issues and refine the structure before submitting it for publication.

When an alert is generated, it is essential to review the checkcif report thoroughly and make the necessary corrections. Failure to correct the errors could lead to the rejection of the manuscript or publication of incorrect or incomplete structural data.

Therefore, it is good practice to check the quality of crystallographic data with checkcif or other validation tools before submitting them for publication.
user: checkcif alert level G

assistant: In crystallography, a CheckCIF alert level G means that there is an inconsistency with the space-group symmetry reported in the CIF file. The space group is an essential parameter used to describe how atoms are arranged in a crystal structure. If there is a discrepancy in the reported symmetry, it could suggest errors or omissions in the crystal structure determination process.

The G alert level could indicate different types of discrepancies, such as:

- A transformational supergroup of the reported space group has a higher symmetry than the one reported.
- The space group is impossible for the reported Bravais lattice.
- The setting of the reported space group is not consistent with the reported cell lengths or angles.
- The space group is consistent with the intensity data, although the systematic absences are not.

When a CheckCIF alert level G is generated, it is critical to investigate and resolve any discrepancies with the symmetry. This may involve re-analyzing or refining the crystal structure or data to ensure that the correct space group is reported. Ultimately, resolving the CheckCIF alert G will help to ensure the quality and accuracy of the reported crystal structure.

1. Plan ahead: Be proactive and plan your request in advance. Consider the potential impact on your workload and try to pick a time where your absence would cause minimal disruption.

2. Understand their perspective: Put yourself in your boss's shoes and try to understand their reasoning for believing you should be at work. Assess the situation from their point of view to anticipate their concerns and address them effectively.

3. Research company policies: Review your company's policies regarding leave, vacation time, personal days, etc. Ensure you are aware of any specific guidelines or restrictions in place.

4. Choose the right time to discuss: Find an appropriate opportunity to approach your boss for a discussion. Avoid busy or stressful periods and consider scheduling a meeting or asking for a brief chat when they seem more approachable.

5. Prepare your case: Make a thoughtful and convincing case for why you need the day off. Identify valid reasons such as family events, important appointments, personal obligations, or special occasions. Ensure your request is reasonable, and avoid any appearance of prioritizing non-work commitments over your job.

6. Present a solution: Propose potential solutions to mitigate the impact of your absence. Suggest alternative ways to get the work done, such as delegating tasks to a colleague, working extra hours before or after the leave, or offering to be available remotely if possible.

7. Demonstrate your commitment: Highlight your dedication and reliability as an employee. Emphasize your track record of meeting deadlines, completing projects successfully, or going above and beyond when needed. Show that this is a rare request and that your commitment to your work remains high.

8. Address concerns: If your boss expresses concerns about workload or conflicts arising from your absence, address them respectfully. Offer solutions or compromises to alleviate those concerns.

9. Follow proper procedure: If your company requires formal leave requests or documentation, make sure you follow the correct procedure and provide any necessary paperwork promptly.

10. Be open to negotiation: Be open to negotiation and flexibility. If your boss cannot grant leave on the specific day, ask for potential alternatives that can work for both parties. Showing willingness to compromise and find middle ground can improve your chances of getting leave approved.

nl:
Bard is a conversational generative artificial intelligence chatbot developed by Google, based initially on the LaMDA family of large language models (LLMs) and later PaLM. It was developed as a direct response to the rise of OpenAI's ChatGPT, and was released in a limited capacity in March 2023 to lukewarm responses, before expanding to other countries in May.

LaMDA had been developed and announced in 2021, but was not released to the public. OpenAI's launch of ChatGPT in November 2022 and its subsequent popularity caught Google executives off-guard and sent them into a panic, prompting a massive and unprecedented level of response in the ensuing months. After mobilizing its workforce, the company scrambled to launch Bard in February 2023, with the chatbot taking center stage during the 2023 Google I/O keynote in May.

Background
In November 2022, OpenAI launched ChatGPT, a chatbot based on the GPT-3 family of large language models (LLM).[3][4] ChatGPT gained worldwide attention following its release, becoming a viral Internet sensation.[5] Alarmed by ChatGPT's potential threat to Google Search, Google executives issued a "code red" alert, reassigning several teams to assist in the company's artificial intelligence (AI) efforts.[6] Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Google and parent company Alphabet, was widely reported to have issued the alert, but Pichai later denied this to The New York Times.[7] In a rare move, Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, who had stepped down from their roles as co-CEOs of Alphabet in 2019, were summoned to emergency meetings with company executives to discuss Google's response to ChatGPT.[8]

Earlier in 2021, the company had unveiled LaMDA, a prototype LLM,[9][10] but did not release it to the public.[11] When asked by employees at an all-hands meeting whether LaMDA was a missed opportunity for Google to compete with ChatGPT, Pichai and Google AI chief Jeff Dean stated that while the company had similar capabilities to ChatGPT, moving too quickly in that arena would represent a major "reputational risk" due to Google being substantially larger than OpenAI.[12][13] In January 2023, Google sister company DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis hinted at plans for a ChatGPT rival,[14] and Google employees were instructed to accelerate progress on a ChatGPT competitor, intensively testing "Apprentice Bard" and other chatbots.[15][16] Pichai assured investors during Google's quarterly earnings investor call in February that the company had plans to expand LaMDA's availability and applications.[17]

Features
Google has made significant enhancements to the global accessibility of Google Bard, expanding its language support to a more diverse range. The update now enables users to use Bard in more languages such as Arabic, Chinese (Simplified/Traditional), German, Hindi, and Spanish, and more. Bard also has included more accessibility options such as a text-to-speech system that allows the AI to read its response out loud to the user.

Google has integrated Bard into many of its products through "extensions", adding a button to fact-check AI-generated responses through Google Search, and allowing users to share conversation threads.[18] Google also introduced the "Google-Extended" web crawler as part of its search engine's robots.txt indexing file to allow web publishers to opt-out of allowing Bard to scan them for training.[19] Online users later discovered that Google Search was indexing Bard conversation threads on which users had enabled sharing. Google stated that this was an error and quickly moved to rectify the leaks.[20]

Bard has taken steps to ensure a safe online environment for teenagers. With improved safety features, Bard is able provide a secure space for young users. The platform now includes advanced content filtering and moderation systems, preventing younger audiences from be shown explicit content or other danger. With a commitment to user safety, Bard has improved technology to identify and restrict access to harmful materials, making Bard a trusted and responsible digital space for teenagers to explore, learn, and connect.

Google has announced the expansion of Bard's ability to understand YouTube videos to including context and content from within the video itself.[21]

History
Announcement
On February 6, 2023, Google announced Bard, a conversational generative artificial intelligence chatbot powered by LaMDA.[22][23][24] Bard was first rolled out to a select group of 10,000 "trusted testers",[25] before a wide release scheduled at the end of the month.[22][23][24] Bard is overseen by product lead Jack Krawczyk, who described the product as a "collaborative AI service" rather than a search engine,[26][27] while Pichai detailed how Bard would be integrated into Google Search.[22][23][24] Reuters calculated that adding ChatGPT-like features to Google Search could cost the company $6 billion in additional expenses by 2024, while research and consulting firm SemiAnalysis calculated that it would cost Google $3 billion.[28] The technology was developed under the codename "Atlas",[29] with the name "Bard" in reference to the Celtic term for a storyteller and chosen to "reflect the creative nature of the algorithm underneath".[30][31]

Multiple media outlets and financial analysts described Google as "rushing" Bard's announcement to preempt rival Microsoft's planned February 7 event unveiling its partnership with OpenAI to integrate ChatGPT into its Bing search engine in the form of Bing Chat,[32][33] as well as playing "catch-up" to Microsoft.[34][35][36] Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told The Verge: "I want people to know that we made them dance."[37] Tom Warren of The Verge and Davey Alba of Bloomberg News noted that this marked the beginning of another clash between the two Big Tech companies over "the future of search", after their six-year "truce" expired in 2021;[32][38] Chris Stokel-Walker of The Guardian, Sara Morrison of Recode, and analyst Dan Ives of investment firm Wedbush Securities labeled this an AI arms race between the two.[39][40][41]

After an "underwhelming" February 8 livestream in Paris showcasing Bard, Google's stock fell eight percent, equivalent to a $100 billion loss in market value, and the YouTube video of the livestream was made private.[34][42][43] Many viewers also pointed out an error during the demo in which Bard gives inaccurate information about the James Webb Space Telescope in response to a query.[44][45] Google employees criticized Pichai's "rushed" and "botched" announcement of Bard on Memgen, the company's internal forum,[46] while Maggie Harrison of Futurism called the rollout "chaos". Pichai defended his actions by saying that Google had been "deeply working on AI for a long time", rejecting the notion that Bard's launch was a knee-jerk reaction.[47] Alphabet chairman John Hennessy acknowledged that Bard was not fully product-ready, but expressed excitement at the technology's potential.[48]

A week after the James Webb debacle, Pichai asked employees to dedicate two to four hours to dogfood testing Bard,[49] while Google executive Prabhakar Raghavan encouraged employees to correct any errors Bard makes.[50] 80,000 employees responded to Pichai's call to action.[25] In the following weeks, Google employees roundly criticized Bard in internal messages, citing a variety of safety and ethical concerns and calling on company leaders not to launch the service. Seeking to prioritize keeping up with competitors, Google executives decided to proceed with the launch anyway, overruling an unsympathetic risk assessment report conducted by its AI ethics team.[51] After Pichai suddenly laid off 12,000 employees later that month due to slowing revenue growth, remaining workers shared memes and snippets of their humorous exchanges with Bard soliciting its "opinion" on the layoffs.[52] Google employees began testing a more sophisticated version of Bard with larger parameters, dubbed "Big Bard", in mid-March.[53]

Launch
Google opened up early access for Bard on March 21, 2023, in a limited capacity, allowing users in the U.S. and UK to join a waitlist. Unlike Microsoft's approach with Bing Chat, Bard was launched as a standalone web application featuring a text box and a disclaimer that the chatbot "may display inaccurate or offensive information that doesn't represent Google's views". Three responses are then provided to each question, with users prompted to submit feedback on the usefulness of each answer. Google vice presidents Sissie Hsiao and Eli Collins framed Bard as a complement to Google Search and stated that the company had not determined how to make the service profitable.[54][55][56] Among those granted early access were those enrolled in Google's "Pixel Superfans" loyalty program,[57] users of its Pixel and Nest devices, and Google One subscribers.[58]

Bard is trained by third-party contractors hired by Google, including Appen and Accenture workers, whom Business Insider and Bloomberg News reported were placed under extreme pressure, overworked, and underpaid.[59][60] Bard is also trained on data from publicly available sources, which Google disclosed by amending its privacy policy.[61] Shortly after Bard's initial launch, Google reorganized the team behind Google Assistant, the company's virtual assistant, to focus on Bard instead.[62] Google researcher Jacob Devlin resigned from the company after claiming that Bard had surreptitiously leveraged data from ChatGPT;[63] Google denied the allegations.[64] Meanwhile, a senior software engineer at the company published an internal memo warning that Google was falling behind in the AI "arms race", not to OpenAI but to independent researchers in open-source communities.[65] Pichai revealed on March 31 that the company intended to "upgrade" Bard by basing it on PaLM, a newer and more powerful LLM from Google, rather than LaMDA.[66] The same day, Krawczyk announced that Google had added "math and logic capabilities" to Bard.[67] Bard gained the ability to assist in coding in April, being compatible with more than 20 programming languages at launch.[68][69] Microsoft also began running advertisements in the address bar of a developer build of the Edge browser, urging users to try Bing whenever they visit the Bard web app.[70] Google is working to integrate Bard into its ChromeOS operating system and Pixel devices.[71][72]

Bard has extended in many countries and is available in France from 13th July 2023.

Updates and Enhancements
Bard took center stage during the annual Google I/O keynote in May 2023,[73] with Pichai and Hsiao announcing a series of updates to Bard, including the adoption of PaLM 2, integration with other Google products and third-party services, expansion to 180 countries, support for additional languages, and new features.[74] In a stark contrast to previous years, the Google Assistant was barely mentioned during the event.[73] The expanded rollout did not include any nations in the European Union (EU), possibly reflecting concerns about compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation.[75] Those with Google Workspace accounts also gained access to the service.[76] Google attempted to launch Bard in the EU in June, but was blocked by the Irish Data Protection Commission, who requested for a "data protection impact assessment" from the company.[77] In July, Google launched Bard in the EU and Brazil, added support for dozens of new languages, and introduced multiple new personalization and productivity features.[78][79] An invite-only chatroom ("server") on Discord was created in July, consisting of users who heavily use Bard. Over the next few months, the chatroom was flooded with comments questioning the usefulness of Bard.[80]

Reflecting on Bard's launch in an interview with Wired in September, Pichai acknowledged that Google had been "cautious" to release LaMDA because of "the responsibility that comes with getting it right", complimenting OpenAI for ChatGPT's launch and firing back at Nadella's comment about making Google dance.[81] Google released a major update to the chatbot later that month, integrating it into many of its products through "extensions", adding a button to fact-check AI-generated responses through Google Search, and allowing users to share conversation threads.[18] Google also introduced the "Google-Extended" web crawler as part of its search engine's robots.txt indexing file to allow web publishers to opt-out of allowing Bard to scan them for training.[19] Online users later discovered that Google Search was indexing Bard conversation threads on which users had enabled sharing. Google stated that this was an error and quickly moved to rectify the leaks.[20]

In October, during the company's annual Made by Google event in which it announced the Pixel 8 series and the Pixel Watch 2, Hsiao unveiled "Assistant with Bard", an upgraded version of the Google Assistant which was deeply integrated with Bard, following in the footsteps of Amazon's approach with Alexa.[82] When the U.S. Copyright Office requested the public to comment on potential new rules on generative AI technologies, Google argued that when AI tools such as Bard are prompted to generate infringing content, the responsibility should lie with the user, not the developer.[83] Accenture contractors voted to join the Alphabet Workers Union in November, in protest of suboptimal working conditions,[84] while the company filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California against a group of unidentified scammers who had been advertising malware disguised as a downloadable version of Bard.[85][86]

In July, Google implemented significant enhancements to the global accessibility of Google Bard, expanding its language support to a more diverse range. The update now enables users to use Bard in more languages such as Arabic, Chinese (Simplified/Traditional), German, Hindi, and Spanish, and more. Bard also has included more accessibility options such as a text-to-speech system that allows the AI to read its response out loud to the user.

In November, Bard has taken steps to ensure a safe online environment for teenagers. With improved safety features, Bard is able provide a secure space for young users. The platform now includes advanced content filtering and moderation systems, preventing younger audiences from be shown explicit content or other danger. With a commitment to user safety, Bard has improved technology to identify and restrict access to harmful materials, making Bard a trusted and responsible digital space for teenagers to explore, learn, and connect.

On November 21, 2023 Google announced the expansion of Bard's ability to understand YouTube videos to including context and content from within the video itself.[87]

Reception
Bard received mixed reviews upon its initial release.[88] James Vincent of The Verge found Bard faster than ChatGPT and Bing Chat, but noted that the lack of Bing-esque footnotes was "both a blessing and a curse",[56] encouraging Google to be bolder when experimenting with AI.[89] His colleague David Pierce was unimpressed by its uninteresting and sometimes inaccurate responses,[90] adding that despite Google's insistence that Bard was not a search engine, its user interface resembled that of one, which could cause problems for Google.[91] Cade Metz of The New York Times described Bard as "more cautious" than ChatGPT,[92] while Shirin Ghaffary of Vox called it "dry and uncontroversial" due to the reserved nature of its responses.[93]

The Washington Post columnist Geoffrey A. Fowler found Bard a mixed bag, noting that it acted cautiously but could show Internet-influenced bias.[94] Writing for ZDNET, Sabrina Ortiz believed ChatGPT and Bing Chat were "more capable overall" in comparison to Bard,[95] while Wired journalist Lauren Goode found her conversation with Bard "the most bizarre" of the three.[96] After the introduction of extensions, The New York Times' Kevin Roose found the update underwhelming and "a bit of a mess",[97] while Business Insider's Lakshmi Varanasi found that Bard often leaned more into flattery than facts.[98]

In a 60 Minutes conversation with Hsiao, Google senior vice president James Manyika, and Pichai, CBS News correspondent Scott Pelley found Bard "unsettling".[99] Associate professor Ethan Mollick of the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania was underwhelmed by Bard's artistic ineptitude.[100] The Times later conducted a test with ChatGPT and Bard regarding their ability to handle tasks expected of human assistants, and concluded that ChatGPT's performance was vastly superior to that of Bard.[101] NewsGuard, a tool which rates the credibility of news articles, found that Bard was more skilled at debunking known conspiracy theories than ChatGPT.[102]

Contrary to previous findings, responses generated by ChatGPT in response to anesthesia related questions were more accurate, succint, and descriptive, as compared to Bard. Bard exhibited 30.3% error in response as compared to ChatGPT (0% error).[103] Furthermore, the responses from ChatGPT were linguistically superior and the vocabulary was more complex than Bard.
